events_chronological: A sound truck for a fringe presidential candidate circles the city broadcasting his platform to nobody in particular.
An ageing country star records a patriotic anthem while a foreign reporter drifts round the studio talking into a tape recorder.
The city's best loved singer collapses at her own airport welcome and is taken to hospital.
A pile-up on the freeway strands most of the city's musicians and hangers-on together for a whole afternoon.
A gospel singer performs with her choir while her husband negotiates with the candidate's organiser.
A folk trio records together while the man among them sleeps with women from every other storyline.
A quiet young man arrives in the city with a violin case and takes a room from an old widower whose wife is dying.
A waitress who has walked out on her husband keeps trying to get onto any stage that will let her sing.
A girl with no voice at all performs at a men's smoker and is made to strip for the room.
The best loved singer is discharged from hospital and breaks down on stage, rambling at the audience until she is led away.
The country star refuses to appear at the candidate's rally unless his own conditions are met.
The gospel singer sleeps with the folk singer after his set and goes home afterwards to her deaf children.
The widower's wife dies on the ward, and the young man lodging with him never notices.
The organiser assembles the rally by promising every performer something different.
The best loved singer performs at the rally and is shot in front of the crowd by the young man with the violin case.
The country star, hit in the arm, tells the crowd that this is their city and passes the microphone to the waitress.
The waitress gets her stage at last and leads the crowd in a song while the ambulances pull away.
The crowd goes on singing as the camera withdraws over their heads.
nonlinear_category_reason: Every strand keeps its own forward order and nothing is ever shown out of turn in time; the inversions are only between strands running at the same moment, which the telling cuts between sideways. Twenty-four characters move through five days in one city, and the film moves between them rather than backwards.
syuzhet_notes: The telling cuts constantly between two dozen people across five days, usually on a song or a passing car, so consecutive told bullets belong to different lives rather than to different times. Nothing is a flashback.
fabula_notes: The five days are continuous and the ordering follows from who is where. Strands that overlap in time can be ranked either way without changing anything.
